summary: Rollout is live in three of four regions with strong usage, and the customer's own TMS data shows dwell time and on-time pickup improving. The open items are the Canada SSO blocker and turning operational gains into a finance-approved dollar figure before the January COO readout.

indicators.evidence: VP of Network Operations attended, framed the COO readout, and asked for it to be scheduled.
indicators.quote: Sam, put the COO readout on my calendar for the second week of January.

indicators.evidence: Sponsor ties results to shipper scorecards without prompting.
indicators.quote: That's what our shippers measure us on. Two of our biggest accounts have mentioned it in their quarterly reviews with us. Unprompted.

indicators.evidence: VP sponsor, Director-level operational owner, and regional leaders are all involved; regional teams extend workflows themselves.
indicators.quote: Priya's my point on all of this.

indicators.evidence: No turnover or reorganization mentioned for the sponsor or champion. Assumed stable, not confirmed.
Objectives are dock dwell time and on-time pickup, both tied to how shippers evaluate Halden.
indicators.quote: And that's the number I care about, the on-time pickup.

indicators.evidence: Pre-go-live baselines exist for dwell time (2.6 hours) and on-time pickup (88%) from the customer's TMS.
indicators.quote: average dock dwell time was two point six hours in the quarter before go-live

indicators.evidence: Measured improvements from the customer's TMS, but the customer flags lighter volume as a possible factor and the dollar value is not finance-approved.
indicators.quote: September and October were lighter volume than the baseline quarter. So some of the dwell improvement could be volume.

indicators.evidence: The sponsor wants to present the results to the COO himself and insists on customer data.
indicators.quote: I don't want to walk in with a number finance will throw out.

indicators.evidence: Live in three of four regions, 31 of 44 facilities. Canada not yet live.
indicators.quote: Dock scheduling automation is live in three of the four regions

indicators.evidence: Core workflows in daily use; Midwest team extended the exception workflow on its own.
indicators.quote: the Midwest team has basically taken over the exception workflow and made it their own

indicators.evidence: Canada SSO group mapping has been failing for three weeks; likely pushes Canada to January. One regional leader finds two screens cumbersome.
indicators.quote: The SSO integration with their identity provider is still failing on group mapping.

indicators.evidence: Customer sets priorities, makes the January call for Canada, and requests a new capability.
indicators.quote: I'd rather do January cleanly than rush it in during peak.

indicators.evidence: Sponsor asked to scope the yard management module for Gulf yards.
indicators.quote: The yard management module. We've had a lot of trouble with trailer visibility in the Gulf yards. Is that something we could pilot?

indicators.evidence: Shippers recognize the service improvement, but finance has not approved the cost-per-dwell-hour figure needed for a dollar value.
indicators.quote: Our finance team has a rough number for what an hour of dwell costs us, but they haven't signed off on using it.

maturity.rationale: Outcomes are measured against baselines in customer data and the sponsor is taking them to the COO. Reaching Expanding requires Canada live, a finance-approved dollar value, and a scoped yard management pilot.

Improve on-time pickup performance for shippers

kpis.note: Recent volume lighter than baseline quarter.

risks.text: Canada go-live slips to January because of the SSO blocker and the November 15 peak freeze.
Part of the dwell improvement may be lower volume, which would weaken the COO story if not controlled for.
No finance-approved dollar value yet for the January readout.
Regional pushback on usability could spread if the screen fix does not land.

opportunities.text: Yard management pilot for Gulf yards after Canada is live, no earlier than February.
January COO readout puts results in front of the economic buyer.
Shippers raising the improvement unprompted makes Halden a strong reference candidate.

actions.detail: Confirm the right Canada IT owner and get the group-mapping issue resolved by November 1, or lock January as the go-live.

actions.action: Control the dwell comparison for volume
actions.detail: Compare the last 90 days with the same quarter last year so the improvement holds up in the COO readout.

actions.action: Get finance to approve cost per dwell hour
actions.detail: Book 30 minutes with Halden finance to agree the figure and method before any dollar value is shown.

actions.action: Set explicit targets for both KPIs
actions.detail: Agree target dwell time and on-time pickup rates for FY27 so progress can be tracked, not just reported.

actions.action: Scope yard management without starting a pilot
actions.detail: Solutions engineer scopes Gulf yard visibility; pilot start no earlier than February, after Canada.

actions.action: Ship the screen fix and close the loop with the Southeast region
actions.detail: Share the next-release fix with Priya and confirm it addresses the regional concern.

statedFacts: Average dock dwell time fell from 2.6 hours to 1.9 hours in the three live regions (Halden TMS).
On-time pickup rose from 88% to 93% in the same regions (Halden TMS).
412 of 480 licensed users are weekly active; 31 of 44 facilities are live.
Two major shipper accounts raised the improvement in their own reviews.
valueNarrative.draft: In the three live regions, Halden's own TMS data shows average dock dwell time down from 2.6 to 1.9 hours and on-time pickup up from 88% to 93%. Two of Halden's largest shippers have noticed without being asked. Before this goes to the COO, we will control for lighter recent volume with a year-over-year comparison and use a cost-per-dwell-hour figure approved by Halden finance.
caveats: No dollar value is shown until finance approves the method.
Recent volume was lighter than the baseline quarter.

projection.text: If nothing changes, Halden renews and is a strong expansion candidate, provided Canada goes live cleanly and the COO readout lands with finance-approved numbers.
